ai.description: This slender gecko reaches 40 mm SVL. It is orange-brown with dark dorsal spots and a pale tail tip. Distinguishing features include a flattened head and a distinct, unpigmented subcaudal scale row.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus aurantiacus* is best distinguished by its bright orange-yellow underside, a unique trait absent in other Indian congeners which typically have pale bellies.
ai.habitat: The Yercaud Slender Gecko inhabits moist deciduous forests and coffee plantations in the Shevaroy Hills, typically at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yercaud Slender Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on tree trunks and rocky surfaces within its restricted forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemiphyllodactylus aurantiacus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus aurantiacus* is endemic to the Shevaroy Hills in Tamil Nadu, India, typically occurring at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
